correctness.rationale: The exact integer identity F²(X)−X=X(X²−3)(X²−1)³ and F(X)−X=X(X²−3) is verified independently by exact polynomial expansion. For odd p, outside ±1 mod p the last factor is a unit so F²≡X forces F≡X; at ±1 the fixed-point factor is a unit and v_p(F²(x)−x)=3v_p(x∓1), giving disjoint balls of radius p^{−ceil(k/3)}. For p=2 every even x is excluded; odd x has v_2(F−x)=1 and v_2(F²−x)=1+3v_2(x²−1), yielding the all-odd k≤10 region and exactly two classes for k≥11. Counting lifts and dividing the even point count by two gives cycles. Both the finite identity and extensive independent modular direct-iteration tests replayed from the actual packaged verifier; the finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Primary texts most plausibly containing the result were checked. Diene–Salim (2013) computes single-map fixed points over fields and explicitly indicates broader cycle structure is not classified there; Qu–Ding (2014) concerns permutation criteria over prime-power rings, not cycle counts; Medina–Moll–Rowland (2015) gives general valuation machinery but not this exact map; Hutz–Patel (2017) treats different maps over primes; Wang (2025) gives Dickson moments, not iterated dynamics. The sharp all-prime-power two-cycle census, especially the 2-adic transition at exponent eleven, was not found in targeted published searches or accessible own claims. This is best-knowledge originality, not uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: The classical 1993 monograph Dickson Polynomials by Lidl–Mullen–Turnwald was not fully inspected for an implicit iterate classification; equivalence may appear in unindexed number-theoretic dynamics work.
Search result ranking and accessible full text cannot establish uniqueness of mathematical statements.
The polynomial identity is elementary; novelty/value depend on the complete sharp universal census rather than a new general factorization technique.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact two-cycle invariant for the smallest nontrivial odd Dickson polynomial of the second kind, a family with published but incomplete cycle-structure literature. It supplies a complete all-prime, all-level point-set and orbit count rather than a finite table, and identifies the genuinely exceptional two-adic all-odd range through k=10 with a sharp transition at k=11. The cubic p-adic ball scaling, distinction of point counts from cycle counts, and parabolic ±1 root multiplicity give interpretable dynamics beyond an arbitrary computational slice; no broader dynamical theorem is claimed.
